That scientific concept can't be seen, which means that if that villain had a fruit that turned him into it, we wouldn't be able to see it. Rather than being black, he would be invisible. This means that the powers of an invisibility fruit that another character has is closer to being a Logia with that scientific concept than that villain's fruit. That scientific concept is NOT an elemental force, but rather an type of matter. So yes, it is stuff, but we don't know what type of stuff it is. Your link is about gravitational singularities, which is again something hypothetical. We actually don't even know what black holes are, if there is an event horizon or not (which is something recent papers now being to question, even the father of black holes, Stephen Hawking). We think there is a singularity, which is an infinitely small point in the universe with mass. Your link says a singularity is not a state of matter, as in it's not a state normal matter can take. Iron can't become a singularity, but it can be solid and liquid. It's a weird question tbh, because matter has to react in some way if it is compressed into infinity, but this just goes to show how weird singularities are. It does fit the criteria for a Logia, since it's an element in a sense. The problem is that it's hypothetical, meaning we don't know if it even exists at all. We also have no idea what it is or how it behaves. We have only predicted it because we know that a lot of mass is missing in the universe. I hope you learned something. I suggest you watch this video if you find that scientific concept interesting. I sure do :D As for your final question, I have no idea. I've wondered myself, and I guess we won't know unless the author tells us. The author would probably just explain it as Luffy: "It's a mystery element!" A final note: That scientific concept has nothing to do with black holes. They are completely seperate theories that has nothing to do with each other. I guess you could say that it's possible that black holes are formed from that scientific concept, since the gravitational pull on light would be the same resulting in a black hole. This is highly unlikely though and would not make much sense.

I have a couple of things to say. First off, one character is far stronger than you give him credit for, while another is not nearly as strong as you give him credit for. Two other characters are both much stronger than that second one. The only reason that second character is threatening and useful for the ruling organization is his special power. He has a specific type of power, which means he is untouchable without a certain defense. That means he is stronger than any character without that defense and as such can be used by the ruling organization against almost any pirate in the first half of a major region where almost no one uses that defense. The first character, on the other hand, was as strong as the protagonist at the point of their fight. I believe he would have defeated the protagonist, had he not been as cocky. The protagonist barely beat him with the use of both enhanced forms, something not even required to beat that second character once you find his weak spot (liquids), which gives you the power to hit him. Had the first character used water in a hypothetical fight against that second character, he would have beaten him. A second problem is your list of villains/antagonists. Why do you feature several other characters there, when they haven't shown to be "friends" of the main group, or at least help them at certain points? One of those characters is the protagonist's idol and as such a great friend of his, while another is shown to be a friend and rival of that one (some theories even say he is a member of his crew). Another helped a female character at certain points and is also featured in a movie as someone who helps the main group. Sure, it's not canon, but it was written by the creator, which means the characters stay true to their personalities. One character basically sacrificed himself to save the protagonist's brother, which means he is never intended as an antagonist. Also, if that character is featured in your list, why is he not the last one? He is stated several times to be the strongest man alive, so I don't see how others would be able to beat him. And if that second character is the strongest among a specific group, or at least equal to both of the other two in strength, why is he not ranked like it in your list? To answer your question, no, the first character would not fit better in an earlier region. He is too strong and his character is intertwined in politics which is not even introduced until just before his defeat. A fight between the protagonist and the first character in that earlier region would not make any sense for both of them.

They didn't know that Crocodile would be present at the war, which means they never gave out the order. > Crocodile is so strong that he does not need Haki even if he has it. This is just wrong. Haki is basically "the new black" in One Piece. Everybody needs it to fight at a high level, which is evidenced in Luffy's 2 year training. Because it's the only thing he needs to "level up". > As for Lucci, he can transform into a large cat and can use finger pistol... scary, he would be killed in a heartbeat if he was fighting with Crocodile. Why? Transforming into a large cat makes him much faster and stronger. Luffy was able to defeat Crocodile without any of his Gears, while he was destroyed by Rob Lucci until he began using them. Yes, I agree that the Luffy vs Crocodile match was quite ridiculous considering that Luffy had been impaled and dried up before hand, but nonetheless it proved that Luffy's fighting skills were superior to Crocodile's, even without Gears. > Mihawk is still an antagonist or will be in the future Why? It shows that it's at least not a clash between an important and strong character vs random fodder, but nothing more than that.  > survived the clash between him and Whitebeard before the war Whitebeard and Shanks are not enemies. The very reason that Shanks joined at the end of the war was to help Whitebeard. The very reason he did not show up until it was too late was to hold Kaido back from fighting Whitebeard while he was occupied with the Marines. > he could battle with Mihawk and make ties with him with a regular sword even after he lost his arm Which Mihawk stated had become boring. Now I wonder why that would be... > by far the strongest we have seen in the show. How do you even come to this conclusion? Sure, he may have some awesome Haki, but it is evidenced by the fact that Mihawk does not enjoy fighting him anymore than his sword fighting skills are not that great after he lost his arm. The problem is simply so much larger that impairment is a huge threat when the parents are closely related.
